newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia - Africa's first independent republic.
newsitem.headline: Liberia - Africa's first independent republic.

text.p: Liberia, Africa's oldest independent republic, was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 and has become a byword for chaos and mindless slaughter in a volatile continent.

After almost seven years of civil war, its West African neighbours rallied its warlords around a peace plan and three of them will be among a dozen candidates fighting for power through the ballot box on Saturday.
Liberia, a patchwork of ethnic groups like most African nations, enjoyed relative stability until the late 1970s.
The descendants of the slaves ruled and developed a flourishing economy based on iron ore, diamonds, the flagging of ships and rubber from what was once the world's biggest plantation -- Firestone.
In 1980, tension with the descendants of tribes who were there when the freed slaves arrived spilled over into bloodshed.
Master Sergeant Samuel Doe, from the Krahn ethnic group, killed President William Tolbert in a coup and then executed members of his government on a palm-fringed beach.

In late 1989, former civil servant Charles Taylor invaded from Ivory Coast unleashing seven years of civil war which spawned rival ethnic or political factions or alliances and killed well over 150,000 people, many of them civilians.
West African peacekeepers arrived in 1990 but it took over a dozen peace deals to end the fighting.
In April and May 1996, the United States airlifted out foreign nationals by helicopter for a second time in the war during political and ethnic clashes in the capital Monrovia.
These are the key facts about Liberia:
POPULATION: 3.0 million (1995 African Development Bank estimate). Descendants of freed American slaves or 16 tribes from four main ethnic groups.
RELIGION: Christians, Moslems, traditional African beliefs.
AREA: 111,300 sq km (43,000 square miles) on the Atlantic Ocean with Sierra Leone to the west, Guinea to the north and Ivory Coast to the east.
LANGUAGE: English (official) and some 28 tribal languages.

HISTORY: Freed American slaves landed in 1822 at a harbour later named Monrovia after U.S. President James Monroe. The country declared itself a self-governing republic in 1847. William Tubman was president from 1944 until his death in 1971. His successor, William Tolbert, was assassinated in a 1980 coup led by Master Sergeant Samuel Doe, a Krahn who ended the stranglehold on power of descendants of slaves. Doe and his National Democratic Party of Liberia (NDPL) won elections in 1985 which opposition parties and outside observers said were blatantly rigged. In December 1989 former civil servant Charles Taylor launched an invasion from Ivory Coast with 150 guerrillas. The revolt spread. The United States evacuated Americans and foreign nationals in 1990 as Taylor tried to take the capital. The Economic Community of West Africa States sent in a peacekeeping force, ECOMOG. A rival faction leader tortured Doe to death. Taylor tried to seize Monrovia again in 1992. Nigerian-led ECOMOG thwarted him.

ARMED FORCES: Liberia's national army, the Armed Forces of Liberia (AFL), numbered 5,800 before the war but disintegrated into just another faction. Estimates of faction fighters ranged from 30,000 to 60,000. ECOMOG peacekeepers, now about 12,000, disarmed two-thirds of them. A new national army is envisaged.

ECONOMY: Traditional exports are iron ore, rubber and timber and, to a lesser extent, uncut diamonds, coffee and cocoa. The war shattered the economy. Diplomats say Liberia is technically bankrupt but the seeds of decline were there under Doe. The World Bank suspended operations in 1987, saying it could not control its projects. The International Monetary Fund closed its Monrovia office in 1988 after Liberia failed to maintain minimum debt payments. The legal currency is the dollar, officially at par with the U.S. dollar. The current rate is $1=47 Liberian dollars. A thriving informal economy has been dominated by Lebanese and Indian traders. Liberia's total external debt is estimated at over $2 billion.
